groups.title: How Tailwind's utility-first model works
groups.question: A teammate builds class names like bg-${color}-500 and the colors never appear in production, and two conflicting padding classes on one element behave unexpectedly. Explain how Tailwind generates and applies its CSS.

followUps.Tailwind purges unused classes at build: Why don't dynamically built Tailwind class names work?
followUps.The cascade in Tailwind: last class wins: Two classes on one element set padding. Which one wins and why?

evidence.text: Tailwind scans source files for class names and only generates CSS for the ones it finds.
A class built from pieces at runtime never appears as a full string, so its CSS is not generated.
Use complete class names, for example by mapping each option to a full class string.

notEnough: Only saying Tailwind purges unused CSS.

evidence.text: Each Tailwind utility sets one property.
When two set the same property, the one defined later in the generated stylesheet wins, not the one written later in the class attribute.
Conflicting classes should be avoided or merged with a tool like tailwind-merge.

notEnough: Only saying the last class wins.

misconceptions.text: Says the class written last in the HTML attribute always wins.

groups.title: Design tokens and the theme system
groups.question: Your brand needs custom colors and spacing, and users want a dark mode toggle that works regardless of their system setting. Explain how you would configure Tailwind's theme.

followUps.Customizing the theme: colors, spacing,: Why use extend in the Tailwind config instead of replacing the theme?
followUps.Dark mode with the class strategy and pr: How does the class strategy for dark mode work?

evidence.text: Brand colors, spacing and breakpoints are added in the Tailwind config file.
extend adds new values while keeping Tailwind's defaults.
Replacing the theme removes all default values, which breaks existing classes.

notEnough: Only saying you edit the config file.

evidence.text: dark: classes apply only when dark mode is active.
With the class strategy, dark mode is on when a dark class is on the html element, which code can toggle.
The initial value can follow prefers-color-scheme while still letting users override it.

notEnough: Only saying you add dark: prefixes.

groups.title: Tailwind layout and responsive design patterns
groups.question: You are building a responsive page with a header bar and a card grid that shows one column on phones and three on desktops. Explain how you would do it with Tailwind.

followUps.Responsive breakpoints: mobile-first wit: If sm:flex applies at 640px and up, what applies on smaller screens?
followUps.Flexbox and grid utilities: flex, grid,: When would you use flex utilities and when grid utilities?

evidence.text: Unprefixed classes apply at all screen sizes.
Prefixed classes like sm: and md: apply from that width upward.
You design for small screens first and add prefixed classes for larger ones.

misconceptions.text: Says sm: classes target small phone screens.

evidence.text: flex with alignment classes handles one-direction layouts like a header bar.
grid with column counts and gap handles card grids.
col-span lets one item cover several columns.

groups.title: Reusable component patterns with Tailwind in T3
groups.question: Your Button component accepts extra classes, and passing p-2 when it already has p-4 leaves both on the element. You also want a card's text to change color when the card is hovered. Explain how you would handle both.

followUps.Using clsx and tailwind-merge to compose: What does a cn helper built from clsx and tailwind-merge do?
followUps.Applying variants with the group and pee: How do the group and peer modifiers let one element's state style another?

evidence.text: clsx joins class names conditionally, dropping false values.
tailwind-merge removes conflicting Tailwind classes, keeping the last one passed.
Together they let callers override a component's default classes cleanly.
Adding group to a parent lets children use group-hover to react when the parent is hovered.
peer lets an element style a following sibling based on the peer's state.
These work in CSS alone without JavaScript state.
